claim: In the matching retail DLL, four small Player aftermath helpers reached directly from already-canonical damage paths are closed as independent exact bodies. Player.SetLastDamage (0x06004EDC) has one Float32 parameter named dmg and an exact 8-byte body consisting only of LastDamage=dmg and return. Player.SetLastSkill (0x06004EB1) has one SkillSlotEnum parameter named skill and an exact 26-byte body: it stores lastSkill=skill, clears lastSkillHit to zero, calls plCont_AI.ResetCheckedPriAct(), then returns. Player.Bleeding (0x06004F1F) is parameterless with an exact 50-byte body: it sets Player.isBleeding=1, sets FormRen.isBleeding=1, then increments MatchEvaluation.inst.PlResult[PlIdx].bledCnt by one and returns. Player.SetDownTime (0x06004ED8) has one Int32 parameter named tm and an exact 64-byte body: it stores DownTime=tm, clamps negative values to zero using the emitted signed bge branch, and when MatchUI.inst converts true calls MatchUI.SetGauge_DownTime(PlIdx,DownTime), then returns. FACT-0020 pins SetLastDamage, SetLastSkill and Bleeding caller boundaries; FACT-0021 pins SetDownTime in its S1-rule path; FACT-0026 independently pins SetLastDamage from ProcessCritical.

limits: This fact groups four caller-connected aftermath helpers but does not claim that they share one implementation template.
CAP-R6-001 contains no standalone PRE/POST events for these helpers, so this gate uses exact matching-DLL bodies and already-pinned caller boundaries.
PlayerController_AI.ResetCheckedPriAct and MatchUI.SetGauge_DownTime internals are outside this fact unless separately closed.
The semantic meaning of lastSkill, bleeding counters and down-time remains governed by caller/data provenance; this fact preserves exact field/call behavior only.
